evidence: NESTING (arithmetic on the frozen bytes: Pass). task/tests/test.sh is byte-identical to the frozen template test.sh (diff empty): run_suite gates 1500 (test.sh:213), run_suite scored 11100 (test.sh:224), each wrapped in `timeout $budget_sec rewardkit --max-concurrent-agent 1` (test.sh:207), so dimensions in a suite run sequentially (rewardkit runner.py:319-330 agent semaphore). task.toml tail ([agent] 7200, build_timeout_sec 600, cpus 2, memory 4096, [verifier] 13200) is identical to the template and staged-task-contract.md:54-63. Gates: render batched timeout 600 (1 criterion) + constraints batched 600 (1 criterion) = 1200 < 1500 (300 s margin). Scored: functional mode='individual', timeout=520, 17 criteria; rewardkit 0.1.7 _arun_agent_individual (judges.py:467-490) runs each criterion as its own sequential agent subprocess under asyncio.wait_for(timeout=judge.timeout) (judges.py:538-549), a timeout zeroing only that criterion; polish batched 900 (5 criteria), visual batched 900 (4 criteria). 17x520 + 900 + 900 = 10640 < 11100 (460 s margin, ~27 s per functional criterion). Gates + scored budgets 1500 + 11100 = 12600 < 13200; sum of all judge timeouts 1200 + 10640 = 11840 < 13200 (Internal sheet wording). Liveness: 120 x 0.25 s sleeps plus two 2 s urllib probes (test.sh:42-58,115-125) bound startup at ~510 s only for a hung app, after which test.sh exits before any suite, so it cannot push a graded run past 13200; restart helper 5 s kill + 30 s ready (test.sh:155-182) sits inside restart_mcp HELPER_TIMEOUT_SEC=55 (restart_mcp.py:11, identical to template) inside one 520 s persistence session. Agent 7200 s and build 600 s are template values; the agent Dockerfile is apt (4 packages) + 2 pinned npm globals (express 5.1.0, better-sqlite3 12.4.1 with node22 prebuilds), a short cold build. Provenance: functional/judge.toml comment records the individual-mode switch as the lead's instruction relayed 8 Oct 2026 and 1200->520 as a DECREASE to fit 17 criteria; no budget was increased, so the below-five-hour authorization rule is not engaged. LONG ENOUGH (unmeasured; required evidence missing -> risk). (1) 520 s is derived from arithmetic, not workload: the comment says it was lowered because 6x1200 no longer fit 17 criteria, and KITTLE_BUILD_CONTEXT.txt:19 had planned 1200 s per criterion. REVIEW_POLICY: 'Workload is measured, not inferred from a timeout number.' raw-evidence-index.json scope states 'Full configured grading/workload ... are absent'; the only runtime evidence is the scripted Playwright golden run (golden-run.log, hashes verified, 21:19:50-21:20:54Z, ~64 s for all 21 legs), which the index labels 'Not a ... judge-duration measurement'. (2) Per-session load is heavy: each of the 17 sessions first redoes the global browser gate (functional/prompt.md:11-19: load, sign in as gwen, verify protected content), then multi-account legs with request recording and in-page replays through Playwright MCP (launched --isolated, so separate-user 'tabs or contexts' need extra context work). Examples: signin_and_client_scope (Parts A+B: ~4 account switches, 3 replays, wrong-password check, harriet cross-check), wall_every_route (Sian controls, then Dev with 3 searches, 3 replays, direct transcript URL), unread_and_new_messages_line (Dev in two contexts + Harriet, ten-second live waits, mark-unread, Gwen cross-check), search_and_transcript (Parts A+B plus Dev transcript checks), sent_once_in_order (two replays, search, transcript, two users, reloads). With a flash model over OpenRouter through claude-code, each MCP round trip carrying chat-page snapshots plausibly costs ~8-15 s; 35-50 calls per heavy criterion spans ~300-750 s, straddling 520. The only comparator found (hosted Colderwater run run-outputs/coldwater-playground-devtools/runs-export/run-75888fe5.../result.json, verifier 08:21:34-09:29:53Z, ~68 min) used one BATCHED functional session, a different shape, so it does not measure per-criterion individual-mode duration here. (3) The cost of a too-short timeout is amplified: a timed-out criterion scores 0 (judges.py:285-300), which can drop the golden below the 0.95 Oracle target, and state-mutating criteria cascade - timer_changes step 3 restores M-13 to 30 days and wall_added_live lifts Sian's wall; a kill before those steps leaves later criteria (persistence notes M-13's timer; search_and_transcript; live_updates_keep_my_work on M-13) judging altered state. (4) Parse-failure retries (judges.py:229 _MAX_JUDGE_RETRIES=3; loop at 532-566) give each retry a fresh 520 s wait, so one pathological criterion can consume up to 1560 s; a single such case exceeds the 460 s margin and the outer `timeout 11100` kills the scored suite, after which score.py:38-48 yields reward 0 for every submission. That is standard rewardkit behaviour, not a task defect, but it makes the thin per-criterion headroom relevant. Plausible broken app passing / conforming app failing: a broken app gains nothing from these timeouts (timeouts only zero criteria). A conforming app (the golden) can lose credit if heavy criteria exceed 520 s with the configured judge - a credible, unmeasured risk rather than a demonstrated defect. No Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
counterexample: Not demonstrated (verdict is Not exercised, not Fail). Credible scenario: the configured claude-code judge with z-ai/glm-5.3-flashx spends >520 s on signin_and_client_scope or unread_and_new_messages_line against the golden; that criterion is zeroed (judges.py:543-549), and if a kill lands in timer_changes before its step 3, M-13 stays at 'off' so persistence and later M-13 checks diverge, pulling the golden below 0.95.
suggested_fix: Before freezing, run the full configured verifier (gates + scored, REWARDKIT_JUDGE=claude-code, REWARDKIT_MODEL from task.toml) against the golden at least once and record per-criterion wall time from the functional session output; if any criterion approaches ~70% of 520 s, reduce or split legs (keeping public scope consistent) or trim criterion count so a larger per-criterion timeout fits within 11100. Do not change test.sh budgets or the verifier timeout. Bind the measurement to the candidate hash in the raw evidence index.
